aria: Animated recap of the Timberwolves' 113 to 106 road win over the Thunder: Ayo Dosunmu's 3-pointer with 1:30 left that made it 110 to 104, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jaden McDaniels' 32 points, the top scorers, how the Timberwolves won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from StatMuse's game page for the Timberwolves' 113–106 win at Oklahoma City on Nov 25, 2026, an NBA Cup group game: all 113 Minnesota points and all 106 Oklahoma City points add up from the player lines, as do the threes (17 of 39 to 11 of 33), free throws (16 of 24 to 11 of 18) and assists (25–20); field goals made (40–42) are on StatMuse, DigestSports and VAVEL. The quarter scores (26–21–40–26 to 16–37–30–23), 53–47 Oklahoma City at the half and 87–83 Minnesota after three are on StatMuse, VAVEL and OKC Thunder Wire; Heavy and 95.3 The Score also have 87–83. Fast-break points (19–7) and points in the paint (44–46) are on StatMuse and Fadeaway World. The biggest leads (Minnesota 12, Oklahoma City 11) are from StatMuse; Heavy and 95.3 The Score have Oklahoma City up 74–63 in the third. Team rebounds, blocks and turnovers differ between sources by one or two and are not shown. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Jaden McDaniels had 32 points on 11 of 15, 10 rebounds, 5 assists and no turnovers, his second straight 30-point game after a career-high 34 against Brooklyn on Monday, and scored 17 in the third quarter as Minnesota closed it on a 24–9 run (Heavy; 95.3 The Score). Minnesota is 3–0 in NBA Cup group play and has won three straight and 10 of 12; Oklahoma City has lost three straight and seven of nine and finished group play 2–2 (95.3 The Score; The Oklahoman). LaMelo Ball left with 2:29 left with a left ankle injury and did not return (The Oklahoman; 95.3 The Score; DAZN). Minnesota played without Anthony Edwards (knee) (DAZN); Oklahoma City without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, among others (The Oklahoman). Ayo Dosunmu scored 13 in the fourth (VAVEL). Next: Minnesota hosts Memphis on Friday at 8:30 PM ET in the NBA Cup (DAZN; Ball Exclusives); Oklahoma City visits Milwaukee on Saturday (The Oklahoman).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Ayo Dosunmu's 3-pointer with 1:30 left that made it 110–104: StatMuse's play-by-play has "A. Dosunmu makes 23' three / Assisted by T. Shannon Jr." at 1:30 for 107–104 to 110–104 (DigestSports' play-by-play has the same play as a 22-footer), and OKC Thunder Wire calls it the "corner 3" that effectively ended Oklahoma City's chances. So the board's Wolves +3 to +6 is 107–104 to 110–104. The defender isn't named, so it is drawn as the template's plain catch-and-shoot pull-up from about 23 feet. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Minnesota Timberwolves or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Ayo Dosunmu's 2021 draft combine measurements: 6-foot-5 in shoes, 194 pounds and a 6-foot-10.25 wingspan (nbadraft.net), in Minnesota's road kit with No. 13 (Land of Basketball) and the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
